_comment:
Closes the hole in the witness check. A witness's death used to be an annotation on the charter's own witness list, so a forger who simply declined to write obiit defeated the whole test by omission. Deaths live out here now, in a book he never touched.

NOTE what this is NOT. It is not a necrology of the Empire, because a complete one would be an oracle and an oracle ends the game. It is four extracts in four hands: each covers one house, each is written up only so far, each reckons in its own house's style — and three houses return nothing at all, with the reason printed on the page beside them. Absence from these rolls is NEVER evidence of life.

The Saint Wend extract is reckoned from ELECTION. A clerk who reduces it as an imperial notary would will lay its men in the grave later than they went into it. That is fair rather than cruel only because the roll states its own reckoning in its own note, on its own page.

Matching is on person_id and never on the name. Two men may be called Hugo Wend, and one of them is in nobody's roll at all.

book.title: The Kalendar of the Dead
book.subtitle: obits returned to this Chancery, and by whom
book.front_matter:
This Chancery keeps no roll of its own dead and never has. What it keeps is this book, which is not a necrology but a binding of extracts: what the houses that do keep such rolls have returned to us, copied in the order their own books were written, with the hand named at the head of each.

Read the head before you read the names. Every hand counts an emperor's years as its own chancery counts them, and says so on its own page, and one of these four does not count as we do.

Read the covering line also. It says whose dead that house undertook to keep, and no more than that. A man who is not in a roll is not thereby living; he may only be a man that roll was never keeping.
book.marginalia: Four houses answer and three do not. In eleven years at this desk I have never once been able to write down that a man was living — only that nobody has sent word he was dead. — R.V.

rolls.hand: The Cathedral Chapter of Saint Wend
rolls.covers: the clergy of this diocese and its lay confratres
rolls.note: This church counts the years of an emperor from the day he was chosen, as it has always done, and it did not begin doing so in order to inconvenience your office. A clerk who reduces these years by his own accession will lay every man in this roll in his grave a year or three after he went into it.
rolls.marginalia: Election. Say it aloud before you open the Almanac, because you will not think to say it after. — R.V.

entries.name: Adalbero
entries.title: dean of the chapter
entries.note: Dean one-and-thirty years. He left his psalter to the school and his mule to the porter.

entries.name: Volkmar Ise
entries.title: deacon of the Nether Fen
entries.note: Drowned at the ford at Grellenbach, going out to a sick man in the dark.

entries.name: Irmingard Fust
entries.title: consoror of this church
entries.note: Gave the chapter her house by the north door and was buried beneath it.

entries.name: Notker of Vitz
entries.title: precentor
entries.note: Precentor two-and-thirty years, and had no voice at all for the last nine of them.

rolls.covers: the Margrave's household and the ministeriales
rolls.note: A house that breaks a die before witnesses on the day its holder dies learns very quickly to write the day down. These years are the Chancery's own, counted from the accession, and this chapel will stand behind every one of them.
rolls.marginalia: This roll and the Book of Matrices put Dietrich in the same year, which is the only time two sources in this office have ever agreed without being made to. — R.V.

entries.name: Eckhard von Melle
entries.title: marshal of Thurn
entries.note: Marshal four-and-twenty years. Died at Marchfeld in the same season as the Emperor, and was carried home.

entries.name: Dietrich
entries.title: Margrave of Thurn
entries.note: His die was defaced in this chapel the same day, before nine witnesses, as the March requires.

entries.name: Folkwin Tanne
entries.title: forester of the Vech
entries.note: Taken by the water at the alder bank. Six weeks in the finding of him.

rolls.covers: enrolled burgesses and sworn masters of the guilds
rolls.note: The council keeps no roll of the dead. It keeps the roll of the city, and strikes a man out of it in the week it is told he is gone, and the book is copied to Aachen-Verd every Michaelmas whether the Chancery has asked for it or not.
rolls.marginalia: The commune strikes a man out the week he dies and never says of what. Two years ahead of the Church and half a sentence behind it. — R.V.

entries.name: Reinmar Vogt
entries.title: master cooper of the guild
entries.note: Struck out at the Michaelmas sitting. The coopers chose his successor the same evening.

entries.name: Vincke Sarwart
entries.title: master of the armourers
entries.note: Struck out the winter after the Emperor died — which is why he stands under Kunrad and Nadler under Aldric.

entries.name: Osanna Peck
entries.title: burgess in her own right
entries.note: Enrolled in her own right after her husband died. The city permits this; Hallenstein does not.

rolls.covers: our own clerks, and the Emperor's household at Verd
rolls.note: Kept by the steward of the house, who counts an emperor's years from the accession and would be astonished to be told that anybody counts them otherwise. He enters a man on the day the bed is stripped.
rolls.marginalia: Two hands held this desk before me and both of them are on this page. The office records what a man wrote and what he was paid for the writing, and nothing whatever about the mornings in between. — R.V.

entries.name: Isenbard Kliff
entries.title: notary at the third desk
entries.note: Eight years at the desk. Died in the lodging under the stair, of the winter cough.

entries.name: Petrissa Sill
entries.title: keeper of the wax
entries.note: Kept the wax and the resin two-and-twenty years, and left the office four marks for candles.

entries.name: Christof Ulner
entries.title: scribe of the writing office
entries.note: Copied the office ordinances out fair in his last winter. Nobody has read them since.

entries.name: Fulco Tresch
entries.title: doorkeeper
entries.note: Doorkeeper thirty years. His stool is still in the passage and nobody sits on it.

silent.reason: Ostmark is partible: Berthold's four sons keep four foundations and four kalendars between them, and no one of them will answer for the dead of a Duchy that is already in quarters.
The Count keeps a roll and will not send it — R.V. wrote to Ulrich four times and had one reply, which said that the dead of Hallenstein are Hallenstein's affair.
The Wends keep no writing of any kind, and the few extracts a clerk once made for us burnt with the archive at Lenz in '18.
